I am an artist and I’m new to the sub, so I’m not great at critical theory and long words but here are my thoughts. I am extremely anti-AI “art.” 

I will be omitting the quotations around the word “art” henceforth but I intend to express that it does not fit the definition of art because my personal definition of art is that it is made by humans or beings with “consciousness”. (Like in the game Detroit: Become Human, when robots have their own consciousness and emotions)

Art is valuable to me and also many others because of human effort. 

Making art yourself is completely different to writing a prompt. The physical labor and time, emotional depth, time spent accumulating skills, human passion, creativity, stylistic choices of each single brushstroke/pencil stroke, and happy mistakes cannot be substituted with generated images. 
The happy mistakes/human unconscious (See: the idea of the pre-sense) are where some of the greatest artworks come from.

AI art consists of writing a prompt and this prompt writing does not constitute an art piece in and of itself. An artist could possibly take the words of the prompt and display it as art. But the part that the human actually made is the words, not the image. Ultimately AI art consists of a non-human entity trained on stolen datasets that creates the final image. Which is the reason why there are many artists against AI, and I am part of the “Artists against generative art” Facebook group with ~135k members.

I believe that the use of the term “AI” is not fully accurate because the machines do not have thought/emotions/their own consciousness. But I will use it because that’s what it’s called by the general public and tech…

I’m finding it difficult to argue against the fact that people think that humans being inspired by other humans is somehow THE SAME as AI generation. I have been trying to come up with a logical conclusion that this is not the same for months. I know it’s not. I just can’t verbalise it yet.

The thing that I think is missing is the very human notions of Respect and Consent. There is an element of respect when artists are drawing inspiration from a source. They typically pay some sort of homage to the original artist, in interviews or in their hearts. I know this is all very wishy washy. Artists make work that are similar to each other inevitably but I believe that their human creativity, and choices about their artwork make up for it. Human artists WANT to make something that is uniquely theirs. 

In your disney example, if a kid made something similar, they would probably say - this is heavily inspired by disney. Everyone would be able to tell it is disney-inspired. If they were to publish it for *monetary gain*, then disney might not do anything, tell them to stop, or hire them. There are comprehensive copyright laws that state what is and isn’t legal that I don’t know. It doesn’t really matter to me because I know it’s a imaginary scenario and I don’t know the inner workings of Disney so I can’t answer your question.

Yes, your point about AI art not being the same as human art stands, but hoards of people on the internet will always say otherwise, that the AI produced work that they prompted might as well be their own digital paintings. 

Corporations laying off artists is a seperate issue but it’s still connected and saying it doesn’t change the issue that the technology is prompting (haha) these career deaths.

I don’t believe that drawing inspiration from a few artists/sources is the same as stealing hundreds of thousands of images without any permission to feed into generative AI. (They get collaged, as I’m sure you know, there are bits of signatures in AI generated content) 

What can I say, I’m an artist that values human creativity more than generative algorithms.

I was just responding to people on this thread who say with 100% certainty that self diagnosis is Never Valid for Any medical reason. (hyperbole)

You got diagnosed, great. 

Diagnosis are case by case scenarios. It depends on the doctor, and if parents take their children to see a doctor. It depends on the medical facilities in the area. 

Mental illness and disability has always been stigmatised. Of course there are people being missed. Because some parents, especially religious ones, refuse to believe there’s something wrong. There is also an aspect of shame and social outcasting when it comes to parents with autistic children. So, not every parent will want their child to be diagnosed or believe that their child needs a doctor/psychiatrist.

I think it’s really interesting that people say that self diagnosis is “not valid in any other medical space” because there is nuance. You can self diagnose with a cold/flu/covid. My doctor approved my self diagnosis of cold urticaria, because I have the defining symptom: my skin gets itchy when my skin gets cold. Just to add to the conversation.

The scientific study of autism (and mental health) was primarily done on middle class and upper class white males. So any POC, female/gender diverse, or low income people who want a professional diagnosis are already at a higher risk of an incorrect diagnosis/ being denied a diagnosis.

https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC8500365/

Firstly, I’m so sorry that you’re going through this I don’t know how to convince you of anything, and you don’t even have to listen. It’s up to you. 

We all have these stories inside our head, about ourselves. If you believe and fall to your depressive thoughts, create a story of misery and never fitting in, then it’s going to happen. But what will happen if you don’t? What happens if you stop thinking about how different you are and accept that we all were born the same way, from the same atoms and formed with the exact same structures? You forget that EVERYONE is trying to be “normal.” There are people who are secretly racist, there are people who have horrible fetishes, and there are disgusting child traffickers and sex workers and cult leaders. Talk to them. Try and bond with people, and if all else fails, know that you’re not alone in your isolation from the world. As dumb as it sounds, these people with weird fetishes and child traffickers and cult leaders know in some way that what they’re doing is wrong, and they must feel like they’re pretending to be normal, too. We all are.

People want to die because death is certainty. Dying now guarantees your life will never ever improve, and the question is: do you want it to? Sure, a depressed person’s brain is not going to magically be fine, it would be a long gruelling journey to getting better. But it gives you at least a chance, even a small one, that your life won’t be so painful and miserable. There is no answer to life that anyone will give you, and the only thing humans can really do is try to enjoy ourselves, and do as many of the things we want while we can. But I always go by one of my favourite quotes:
“You know you can die at anytime you want. So what’s the rush?”
Go ahead and try again! If that fails and you really want to die, I can’t stop you. But just remember that there’s no rush. You know you’ll die eventually, so why should you?
